summary: Axial CT pulmonary angiography with a source-described saddle embolus.
text: A saddle embolus occupies the pulmonary arterial bifurcation and extends into branches on both sides. Look for the intraluminal filling defect within the contrast-enhanced pulmonary artery. The descending thoracic aorta provides a separate posterior vascular landmark.
reading: Distinguish the pulmonary arterial circulation from the descending aorta.

questions.prompt: How does the infarcted region appear on the DWI image in this four-hour source case?
questions.explanation: The source comparison shows a conspicuous DWI abnormality and lower ADC in the infarcted basal ganglia, while conventional T2 did not reveal the region clearly.

labels.note: Restricted diffusion (bright on DWI) in the left basal ganglia: the hyperacute infarct, four hours after onset. It lies over the lentiform nucleus and adjacent deep grey matter, and corresponds to the lower-ADC region in the paired ADC case.
Normal right lentiform nucleus, the unaffected comparison side.
Left lateral ventricle (temporal horn region), a dark CSF space on the scan.
Right lateral ventricle, the normal side for comparison.

summary: Axial DWI in the source's four-hour basal ganglia infarction case.
text: The infarcted basal ganglia region is bright on this diffusion-weighted image. The paired four-hour ADC case shows the same patient and infarction, with a lower apparent diffusion coefficient in the corresponding region. The conventional T2 comparison did not show the infarction clearly.
reading: Identify the bright regional DWI abnormality.
Relate its location to the basal ganglia.
Compare it with the lower-ADC region in the paired four-hour ADC case.
